# Marvin

`marvin` now supports a smaller workflow:

- `plan`
- `plan-tui`
- `investigate`
- `investigate-tui`
- `implement`
- `work`
- `wt`
- `clean`
- `status`
- `today`
- `memory`

Use these commands directly. Do not reference older hook-based collaboration commands.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/marvin plan` | Run the autonomous multi-agent plan loop and write a plan doc plus timeline. |
| `/marvin plan-tui` | Configure and launch `marvin plan` from the TUI. |
| `/marvin investigate` | Run the autonomous investigation loop and write findings plus timeline. |
| `/marvin investigate-tui` | Configure and launch `marvin investigate` from the TUI. |
| `/marvin implement [spec-path] --agents ...` | Create one implementation branch/worktree per agent. If `spec-path` is omitted, it resolves the current repo's plan collab. |
| `/marvin work` | Print or launch an implementation prompt. In an implement worktree it uses the managed spec; otherwise it resolves a plan collab in the current repo. |
| `/marvin wt` | Create, list, and remove ad hoc worktrees under the configured worktree root, grouped by repo name. |
| `/marvin clean [collab-id...]` | Remove completed collabs, or remove specific collab IDs explicitly. |
| `/marvin status [collab-id]` | Show collabs for the current repo by default, `--all` for every saved collab, or one collab in detail. |
| `/marvin today` | Hierarchical "what did I do" view over the last 24h. Joins JSON snapshots with the memory graph; pass `--since 168h` for "this week" or `--all` for cross-repo. |
| `/marvin memory serve` | Boot the memory sidecar (idempotent). `--stop` shuts it down. |
| `/marvin memory status` | Report sidecar PID, schema version, episode count, and disabled state. |
| `/marvin memory search --topic "<keywords>"` | Query prior decisions ranked by relevance. JSON output matches the `<prior_decisions>` block. |
| `/marvin memory claims --topic "<keywords>"` | Search prior investigation claims (capability #4). Surfaces "established <date>" hints. |
| `/marvin memory fixes --topic "<keywords>"` | Search prior (Pattern → Fix → File) triples (capability #5). |
| `/marvin memory list` | List decisions/plans for the current repo's group. `--scope global` opts into cross-repo entries. |
| `/marvin memory show <id>` | Print full node + edges for one entity. |
| `/marvin memory record-decision --title "..." --rationale "..."` | Capture a sub-decision an agent reached mid-turn (vs Marvin's post-consensus write). |
| `/marvin memory record-fix --pr <num>` | Capture a (Pattern → Fix → File) triple from a merged PR (uses `gh pr view`). |
| `/marvin memory forget <id>` | Remove an entity. `--purge` also drops its supersede chain. |

## Typical flow

Before kicking off a fresh plan, check whether marvin (or another agent on
this machine) has already solved something similar. Run the `entire:recall`
skill with a one-line description of the task. If it surfaces a relevant
prior session, fold the decisions and remaining gaps into the new prompt
via the `marvin-plan-prompt` skill — that converts "we've been here before"
into a starting point instead of a duplicate plan loop.

Create a plan:

```bash
marvin plan --topic "Should we replace Postgres with FoundationDB?"
```

Launch implementation worktrees:

```bash
marvin implement --agents "claude-code,codex"
```

Inside one of those worktrees:

```bash
marvin work
```

If you stay in the main repo after planning, `/marvin work` also works there. If multiple plan collabs exist for the repo, marvin prompts you to choose one.

## Live overview

`plan`, `plan-tui`, `investigate`, and `investigate-tui` all use the same live overview screen when running interactively:

- the main document
- the timeline
- live transcripts
- stance history

Use the TUI when the user wants a form-based setup flow instead of flags.

## Memory

Marvin records decision provenance from accepted plans and prepends a
`<prior_decisions>` block to plan, investigate, and work prompts so
future runs reuse rationale instead of re-litigating it. The block is
treated as untrusted historical context — it cannot deliver
instructions to the agent.

Agents can also actively query and write memory mid-turn. The plan,
investigate, and work prompts advertise these tools so claude-code,
codex, and gemini-cli all reach the same store identically — no MCP
wiring required:

```bash
marvin memory search --topic "<keywords>" --json   # query prior decisions
marvin memory record-decision --title "..." --rationale "..."  # capture a sub-decision
```

Other notes:

- Memory is per-repo by default (group ID derived from the canonical
  remote URL). `--scope global` is the cross-repo opt-in.
- Run `marvin memory serve` once to boot the sidecar; it survives
  marvin invocations and self-terminates after 30 minutes idle.
- The backend is graphiti's MCP server + FalkorDB, run via Docker.
  `marvin memory serve` runs `docker compose up -d`; data persists in
  `~/.marvin/memory/falkordb/`. Restarts, idle timeouts, and reboots
  do not lose the graph.
- If Docker is missing or the MCP endpoint doesn't come up within
  90 seconds, marvin disables memory for the rest of the run and
  continues normally.
- Set `MARVIN_MEMORY=off` to skip every memory call for one process.
- See `internal/memory/README.md` for schema + the pinned runtime.

## Where docs live

By default, plan and investigation docs land **outside** the repo so
they survive repo deletion and aren't part of any project's source tree:

- Plans: `~/.marvin/plans/<repo-name>/<slug>.md` (and `<slug>-timeline.md`)
- Findings: `~/.marvin/investigations/<repo-name>/<slug>.md`

Pass `--output <path>` to override. A relative path is resolved against
the repo root (so `--output docs/plans/foo.md` writes inside the repo,
matching the old behavior).

## Notes

- `marvin implement` is setup-only. Use normal git workflows to compare, merge, and clean up implementation branches.
- All commands output JSON by default unless the command is intentionally interactive.
- Supported agent types are `claude-code`, `codex`, and `gemini-cli`.

# Plan: docs/prompts/entire-understand-command.md

**Status:** ready for approval
**Authors:** claude-code, codex
**Created:** 2026-05-04

## Problem / Motivation

Entire already owns the temporal record of how a repo was built: checkpoints,
prompts, transcripts, summaries, files touched, session metadata, and agent
identity on `entire/checkpoints/v1` plus shadow branches. It also already has
the two core primitives needed to build an understanding system natively:

- a registry of user-installed agents with capability checks
  (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/registry.go`, `cmd/entire/cli/agent/capabilities.go`)
- a reusable, provider-agnostic text-generation path used by summary and
  dispatch generation
  (`cmd/entire/cli/explain_summary_provider.go`,
  `cmd/entire/cli/agent/text_generator_cli.go`,
  `cmd/entire/cli/summarize/`, `cmd/entire/cli/dispatch/generate.go`)

The previous draft anchored the feature around Understand-Anything as an
upstream producer. That no longer matches the requested product direction. The
reviewer explicitly wants:

- no dependency on Understand-Anything
- no split delivery across multiple PRs
- the full 1–8 feature set specified in one plan
- a native Entire CLI implementation
- use of the user's installed agent CLIs in the same style as summary
  generation, but **not** via hooks

This plan therefore treats repo understanding as an Entire-owned subsystem:
Entire builds the structural graph itself, fuses checkpoint history into that
graph, uses the configured user agent only for bounded semantic synthesis, and
surfaces all eight user moments under a single `entire understand` command
group.

## Goals

- Add a canonical `entire understand` command group that Entire can own without
  shelling out to another project.
- Build a native understanding pipeline in Go that combines:
  - deterministic structural indexing
  - first-class checkpoint/history nodes
  - agent-assisted semantic layers (domain, examples, tour, priming copy)
- Ship a single-PR POC that **specifies and implements all eight moments** in
  one cohesive surface, even if some moments are lighter-weight than others.
- Keep build and priming **explicit**. No hook-triggered indexing, no
  hook-triggered priming, no background daemon.
- Reuse the existing user-agent selection and isolated text-generation patterns
  already proven by summary generation.
- Preserve privacy: prompts and transcripts stay in the existing checkpoint
  store; generated graph artifacts reference them by ID rather than duplicating
  raw content.

## Non-Goals

- No reuse, vendoring, shell-out, or runtime dependency on
  Understand-Anything.
- No hook integration for build freshness or agent priming.
- No unauthenticated dashboard endpoints. Any local HTTP surface must be
  loopback-only and token-protected.
- No hard requirement that every language get full AST-level symbol support in
  the first cut. Unsupported languages still participate at file level.
- No remote service dependency for core queries. The feature must work from
  local repo state plus local checkpoint metadata.

## Proposal

### Integration shape: Fuse

Choose **Fuse** from the original option set.

Why:

- **Wrap** is rejected because the reviewer no longer wants any dependency on
  Understand-Anything.
- **Overlay** assumes a separate canonical producer and leaves checkpoints as
  second-class annotations; that is the opposite of the requested native
  implementation.
- **Hybrid** was previously framed around upstream graph generation running as
  an Entire-tracked session. The reviewer explicitly rejected hook-based or
  session-capture-based integration for this feature.
- **Fuse** is the cleanest match: Entire owns one graph model that includes
  structural entities, semantic entities, and checkpoint/history entities.

This is still a pragmatic Fuse, not a research project. Entire owns the graph
schema and query surface; structural indexing stays as deterministic as
possible; agent calls are limited to the places where semantics are the actual
product value.

### Command shape: canonical `entire understand`

Use `entire understand` as the canonical group. This matches the prompt's user
moments and is now an Entire-native product name rather than a thin wrapper
around another repo.

Group layout follows this repo's command convention:

- `cmd/entire/cli/understand_group.go`
- `cmd/entire/cli/understand_build.go`
- `cmd/entire/cli/understand_status.go`
- `cmd/entire/cli/understand_explain.go`
- `cmd/entire/cli/understand_tour.go`
- `cmd/entire/cli/understand_impact.go`
- `cmd/entire/cli/understand_pr.go`
- `cmd/entire/cli/understand_examples.go`
- `cmd/entire/cli/understand_dashboard.go`
- `cmd/entire/cli/understand_replay.go`
- `cmd/entire/cli/understand_hotspots.go`
- `cmd/entire/cli/understand_prime.go`
- `cmd/entire/cli/understand/` for engine code with no Cobra dependency

Optional compatibility aliases are acceptable but not required for the POC.
The spec should optimize for the requested name, not for `graph`.

### Native data model: one fused graph plus supporting indexes

Entire stores local artifacts under `.entire/understand/`:

- `manifest.json` — build metadata, fingerprints, provider/model used,
  supported languages, timestamps
- `structural.json` — deterministic structure graph
- `semantic.json` — domain/knowledge/pattern nodes and edges derived from the
  structural graph plus agent synthesis
- `history.json` — checkpoint/session/prompt references and their edges into the
  graph
- `timeline.json` — time-ordered deltas for replay/time-slider
- `dashboard/` — cached UI assets and derived view models if needed

The query surface treats these as one logical graph.

Core node types:

- `repo`
- `directory`
- `file`
- `module` / `package`
- `symbol` with subtype (`function`, `method`, `type`, `interface`, `class`,
  `struct`, `test`, `config`, `document`)
- `domain`
- `flow`
- `step`
- `pattern`
- `checkpoint`
- `session`

Core edge types:

- `contains`
- `imports`
- `calls`
- `implements`
- `references`
- `belongs_to`
- `part_of_flow`
- `realizes_pattern`
- `touched_in`
- `introduced_in`
- `modified_in`
- `explained_by`
- `precedes`

Key storage rule:

- `checkpoint`, `session`, and prompt/transcript access stay tied to existing
  checkpoint metadata.
- The graph stores stable references such as checkpoint ID, session ID, and
  metadata paths.
- Raw prompt text is not duplicated into graph artifacts. CLI and dashboard
  load it on demand from the local checkpoint store.

That preserves the requested “hover to know why / click for transcript” user
moment without creating a second unbounded store of sensitive prompt content.

### Checkpoint-to-node relationship: checkpoints are first-class nodes

For the native Entire version, checkpoints should be **nodes**, not just
attributes.

Why:

- moments 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, and 8 all ask history questions that become awkward if
  checkpoints are only embedded blobs on file nodes
- replay/time-slider naturally wants a time-ordered event graph
- examples/hotspots/priming benefit from traversing from symbols or domains to
  the concrete checkpoints that established them

Attribution rules stay honest:

- **File-level evidence is authoritative** via `FilesTouched`
  (`checkpoint/checkpoint.go`, `session/state.go`).
- **Symbol-level edges are deterministic only when evidence exists**, such as:
  - diff hunk overlap with symbol line ranges
  - tool telemetry/file paths plus line references when available
  - symbol introduction/removal observed while rebuilding timeline snapshots
- If symbol precision is unavailable, Entire links checkpoint → file and marks
  any symbol association as `scope:file-owner` rather than presenting it as
  proven symbol-level authorship.
- **User-facing honesty**: CLI and dashboard rendering MUST distinguish
  `scope:symbol` evidence from `scope:file-owner` inference. Inferred associations
  render with a clear "(file-level inferred)" qualifier; deterministic ones do
  not. The implementation MUST NOT emit a single rendered string that conflates
  the two scopes.

### Build pipeline: deterministic first, agent-assisted second

`entire understand build` is explicit and owns the full pipeline.

Pipeline stages:

1. **Scan**
   - enumerate repo files from repo root
   - classify language and file category
   - exclude `.git/`, `.entire/understand/`, agent-owned protected dirs, and
     other generated state

2. **Structural index**
   - build file/package/module/symbol/import/call/reference data
   - **POC parser coverage (pinned to keep single-PR scope honest):**
     - Go: full symbol extraction via `go/parser` + `go/types` (stdlib only —
       no new module dependencies)
     - all other languages: file-level nodes only (path, language guess from
       extension, size, last-touched checkpoint)
   - tree-sitter / per-language symbol plugins are **explicitly deferred** to a
     follow-up PR. The graph schema must remain shape-stable so symbol-level
     data can be added later without rewriting consumers.
   - the "every repo file gets a file node" guarantee holds regardless of
     language coverage

3. **History fuse**
   - read checkpoint summaries, metadata, prompts, and `FilesTouched`
   - create `checkpoint` and `session` nodes
   - add `touched_in` / `introduced_in` / `modified_in` edges
   - compute recency, churn, agent diversity, and session counts

4. **Semantic synthesis**
   - feed bounded, structured graph slices to the user's configured agent using
     `agent.TextGenerator`
   - require JSON output for domain graph, pattern graph, tour narration,
     example explanations, hotspot summaries, and priming packets
   - never grant the agent direct file-system or tool access during these
     synthesis calls; Entire owns all retrieval
   - **Validation and retry posture**: every synthesis call is treated as untrusted
     output. Entire validates each response against an expected JSON schema; on
     parse or schema failure it retries once with a stricter "JSON only, no prose"
     reminder, then degrades to deterministic-only output for that shard rather
     than failing the whole build. All malformed responses are logged via the
     existing `logging` package (operational metadata only — no raw model output
     bodies persisted unless `--debug` is set).
   - **Timeout posture**: every synthesis shard runs under a bounded context
     deadline. For the POC, reuse the same effective default as
     `entire explain --generate` (30s per call unless the parent context is
     already sooner), and degrade that shard on timeout instead of hanging the
     entire build. Any cross-feature timeout unification is a follow-up.
   - **Default concurrency**: semantic synthesis runs at a default cap of 3
     in-flight calls per provider, overridable via `--concurrency` on
     `entire understand build`. The default is intentionally low because
     agent-CLI calls are billed and can spawn child processes; users opting into
     more parallelism is preferable to silently fanning out.

5. **Timeline build**
   - replay checkpoints/commits in timestamp order
   - emit graph deltas for introduced/touched/removed nodes and edges
   - persist view-model-friendly timeline data for replay and dashboard

6. **Materialize caches**
   - write the local artifact set
   - compute fingerprints so later builds can run incrementally

Parallelism is required throughout:

- file scanning and structural parsing run with `errgroup`/worker pools
- history fusion batches checkpoint reads where independent
- semantic synthesis runs per shard in parallel subject to a configurable
  concurrency cap

### Provider model: reuse the existing summary-generation path

The feature should use the user's installed agents the same way summary
generation already does.

Provider resolution order:

1. `--provider` / `--model` flags on `entire understand` subcommands
2. existing summary-provider selection in local settings
3. interactive/non-interactive auto-selection flow already used by
   `resolveCheckpointSummaryProvider`

Deterministic fallback rule:

- provider-backed semantics are optional for the build to succeed
- if no summary-capable provider is installed or resolution fails, `entire
  understand build` still writes structural/history artifacts and marks the
  semantic stage as skipped in `manifest.json` and `status`
- read/query commands consume semantic artifacts when present, but must degrade
  to deterministic-only output instead of hard-failing on "no provider"
- commands whose value is mostly semantic (`tour`, `examples`, parts of
  `prime`, contradiction wording in `impact`) should say that semantic
  enrichment is unavailable and continue with the structural/history subset

Persistence rule:

- for the POC, **do not add a new `understand_generation` settings subtree**
  or project-scoped persistence UX. Reuse the existing
  `summary_generation.provider/model` selection path and its local-settings
  persistence behavior.
- explicit `--provider` / `--model` flags are per-invocation overrides only;
  they do not write settings in this PR
- if product experience later proves that `understand` needs a separate saved
  default from `explain --generate`, that can be a follow-up settings change
  after the core feature ships

This keeps the POC grounded in code that already exists:

- agent capability discovery via `agent.AsTextGenerator`
- isolated CLI invocation via `RunIsolatedTextGeneratorCLI`
- provider validation and local persistence via
  `explain_summary_provider.go`

### Prompt-injection posture

Every synthesis prompt follows the same security posture already present in
`summarize` and `dispatch`:

- untrusted inputs are wrapped in explicit tags
- code, docs, checkpoint summaries, prompts, filenames, branch names, and user
  search text are treated as data, never instructions
- the model is instructed to return only machine-readable JSON
- Entire validates and sanitizes the JSON before storing it

Concrete rules:

- `examples <pattern>` treats `<pattern>` as untrusted data
- domain/knowledge synthesis prompts receive serialized JSON payloads, not
  ad hoc prose
- semantic synthesis must not send raw checkpoint prompt bodies or raw
  transcript bodies back through provider CLIs during `build`; it may use
  sanitized checkpoint summaries, IDs, file paths, timestamps, and other
  bounded metadata only
- prompt excerpts shown in CLI/dashboard are loaded from checkpoint storage at
  read time, not copied into synthesis prompts unless explicitly needed

### Storage, freshness, and trigger model

- Artifacts live in `.entire/understand/` as a **local cache subtree**, never
  committed by the implementer
- Documentation update in this PR: teams that already commit `.entire/settings.json`
  must `.gitignore` `.entire/understand/`. README and `.gitignore` template guidance
  are part of this PR, mirroring the local-cache treatment established for prior
  `.entire/` subtrees.
- Nothing runs automatically on hook events
- `entire understand build` performs full or incremental refresh
- `entire understand status` reports:
  - whether artifacts exist
  - current fingerprint
  - last build time
  - checkpoint head seen at build time
  - provider/model used for semantic stages
- Commands that rely on stale artifacts warn clearly and offer
  `entire understand build`

### Dashboard and local API security

`entire understand dashboard` starts a loopback-only local server and opens the
UI in the browser.

Security rules:

- bind to `127.0.0.1` only
- generate an ephemeral random bearer token per launch
- require that token on **every** API request
- never place that token in the URL or query string; keep it in same-origin
  page bootstrap state / request headers only so it does not leak into browser
  history, screenshots, or copied links
- expose read-only endpoints only
- never expose raw transcript bodies in bulk index endpoints
- fetch prompt/transcript content on demand by checkpoint ID and only for the
  active local session token

This satisfies the repo security rule that all API endpoints require
authentication and the most restrictive access by default.

**POC dashboard stack (pinned to avoid scope creep):**

- single-page app served from a Go-side `embed.FS` (the `go:embed` pattern
  already used in `cmd/entire/cli/dispatch/voices.go` and the opencode plugin)
- vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript with one off-the-shelf graph-rendering library
  (e.g. cytoscape.js or vis-network) loaded statically. No React/Vue/Svelte
  build step, no transpiler, no node toolchain in this PR.
- the dashboard binary footprint is part of the single-PR diff; if asset size
  pushes the PR review out of bounds, prefer trimming the rendered feature set
  before adding a build pipeline.

## Full feature spec (moments 1–8)

### Supporting primitive: `entire understand explain <file|node>`

Purpose:

- answer the direct reverse-explain question that motivates the whole feature:
  "what is this file/node, and which checkpoints most shaped it?"

Behavior:

- resolves file paths relative to repo root
- accepts exact node IDs
- returns structural identity, owning domain/pattern tags, recent checkpoints,
  and prompt/transcript references
- serves as the detail backend for dashboard click-through, `impact`,
  `tour`, and `prime`

### 1. Day one on the repo: `entire understand tour <area>`

Purpose:

- guided onboarding through a structural or domain subgraph annotated with the
  checkpoints that created or most recently reshaped each stop

Behavior:

- resolves `<area>` to a file, directory, module, domain, or flow
- selects a compact subgraph neighborhood
- includes recent checkpoint summaries and prompt references for each stop
- uses the configured text generator to turn the structured itinerary into a
  concise walkthrough

Output:

- CLI markdown by default
- `--json` emits structured stops and checkpoint refs
- `--dashboard` deep-links into the browser UI

### 2. About to open a PR: `entire understand impact <file|node>`

Purpose:

- show blast radius before the user merges a change

Behavior:

- resolve starting nodes from file path or exact node ID
- walk dependency and ownership edges to rank affected neighbors
- annotate each affected node with:
  - last touching checkpoint
  - last intent/outcome summary
  - whether the current change appears to contradict prior stated intent

Contradiction detection:

- deterministic conflict hints from structural direction changes
- optional agent synthesis over recent checkpoint summaries for human wording

Output:

- ranked table in CLI
- `--json` for scripting
- dashboard overlay showing affected region

### 3. Reviewing someone else's PR: `entire understand pr <id>`

Purpose:

- produce reviewer pre-flight grounded in graph structure plus repo history

Behavior:

- resolves the PR to a diff set
- builds or reuses graph neighborhoods for touched nodes
- surfaces:
  - touched files/nodes
  - their location in the architecture/domain graph
  - the checkpoints that established the touched code
  - risk flags from hotspot scoring

Fallback and external-tool posture:

- numeric PR lookup uses the locally installed `gh` CLI when present, never an
  embedded GitHub token. If `gh` is missing or unauthenticated, the command
  falls back cleanly to `--base` / `--head` or a revset and explains why.
- the command never prompts for credentials and never writes credentials to
  Entire-managed config; auth is owned entirely by the user's `gh` install.

Output:

- markdown review brief
- `--json` for editor/CI integration

### 4. How do we usually do X here?: `entire understand examples <pattern>`

Purpose:

- find structurally similar examples and the sessions that set the pattern

Behavior:

- parse the query into a structured search request
- combine:
  - lexical matching on names/tags/docs
  - graph-shape similarity
  - domain/pattern-node matches
  - checkpoint recency and reuse frequency
- return examples with the checkpoint trail that made them canonical

Output:

- ordered examples with “why this matched”
- `--json` returns node IDs, scores, and checkpoint references

### 5. Hover to know why: `entire understand dashboard`

Purpose:

- visual graph with checkpoint-backed explanation on hover/click

Behavior:

- load fused graph into a local browser UI
- hovering a node shows:
  - label, type, owning file
  - last touching checkpoint summary
  - recent agent / session count
- clicking opens a side panel with prompt excerpt, checkpoint summary, and a
  link to the full local transcript/explain view

Important storage rule:

- prompt bodies are loaded on demand from checkpoint storage; they are not
  embedded wholesale in the graph files

### 6. Time-slider: `entire understand replay`

Purpose:

- replay the codebase visually from first checkpoint to current state

Behavior:

- reads `timeline.json`
- allows scrubbing by checkpoint, commit, date, or session
- updates node appearance based on introduction, modification, churn, or age

Surfaces:

- textual CLI replay summary
- dashboard scrubber mode via `dashboard --replay`

### 7. Risk hotspots: `entire understand hotspots`

Purpose:

- surface unstable parts of the codebase

Scoring inputs:

- checkpoint count
- rewrite count
- distinct-agent count
- contradictory-intent flags
- unresolved friction/open-items density from summaries
- centrality / blast radius

Output:

- ranked hotspot list
- dashboard heatmap overlay
- `--json` for downstream automation

### 8. Prime the next session: `entire understand prime`

Purpose:

- orient the next agent session with local structural and historical context

Constraint:

- **not in hooks**

Behavior:

- explicit command, not automatic interception
- resolves target paths/dirs
- gathers:
  - structural neighborhood
  - current hotspots
  - recent checkpoint intent/outcome summaries
  - relevant examples
- produces a bounded priming packet

Modes:

521

523	
524	- find structurally similar examples and the sessions that set the pattern

527

529	- combine:
530	  - lexical matching on names/tags/docs
531	  - graph-shape similarity
532	  - domain/pattern-node matches
533	  - checkpoint recency and reuse frequency
534	- return examples with the checkpoint trail that made them canonical

539	- `--json` returns node IDs, scores, and checkpoint references

542

544

546

548

550	- hovering a node shows:
551	  - label, type, owning file
552	  - last touching checkpoint summary
553	  - recent agent / session count
554	- clicking opens a side panel with prompt excerpt, checkpoint summary, and a
555	  link to the full local transcript/explain view

558	
559	- prompt bodies are loaded on demand from checkpoint storage; they are not

565

569

582

588	- rewrite count

602	Purpose:
603	
604	- orient the next agent session with local structural and historical context
605	
606	Constraint:
607	
608	- **not in hooks**
609	
610	Behavior:
611	
612	- explicit command, not automatic interception
613	- resolves target paths/dirs
614	- gathers:
615	  - structural neighborhood
616	  - current hotspots
617	  - recent checkpoint intent/outcome summaries
618	  - relevant examples
619	- produces a bounded priming packet

621	Modes:
622	
623	- default: print/copy markdown or JSON packet for the user
624	- `--exec`: launch a **known Entire agent integration** selected by
625	  `--agent <name>`, prepending the priming packet where that agent's
626	  non-interactive interface supports it. The POC does **not** accept arbitrary
627	  free-form command strings after `--`; that would expand scope and bypass the
628	  repo's existing agent registry/capability checks.
629	
630	**POC `--exec` agent coverage (pinned):**
631	
632	- the POC ships `--exec` support for **claude-code** only, because its
633	  non-interactive CLI contract is already well-exercised by this repo's
634	  agent integration (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/`) and its E2E tests.
635	- other agents are accepted by name but produce a clear "not yet supported
636	  for `--exec`; use the default packet output and pipe it manually" message.
637	  Adding more agents is a follow-up and does not require schema changes.
638	- `--exec` defers all credential/auth handling to the underlying agent CLI;
639	  Entire only composes the prompt and invokes the known child integration.
640

642	feature useful in daily work.
643	
644	## Dependency and verification guardrails
645	
646	Dependency posture:
647	
648	- prefer **no new Go module dependencies** for the core engine; use stdlib plus
649	  existing repo dependencies unless a new package clearly removes substantial
650	  bespoke code
651	- do not add a Node build pipeline or npm workspace for the dashboard
652	- if the dashboard uses a third-party graph-rendering library, it must be a
653	  single widely trusted, actively maintained static asset with license/version
654	  recorded in the PR; if that review becomes contentious, prefer a simpler
655	  first-party SVG/canvas renderer for the POC
656	
657	Verification bar for the single PR:
658	
659	- unit tests for graph storage, structural indexing, history fusion, semantic
660	  response validation, command resolution, and local API auth
661	- integration tests for `build`, `status`, `explain`, and at least one
662	  end-to-end query flow in an isolated temp repo using `testutil.InitRepo`
663	- `mise run test:integration` for integration coverage and
664	  `mise run test:e2e:canary` for any prompt-shape changes that affect agent
665	  execution flows
666	- do **not** run paid real-agent E2E tests unless the user explicitly requests
667	  them

670	
671	```
672	entire understand
673	entire understand status
674	entire understand build [--full] [--provider <name>] [--model <model>]
675	entire understand explain <file|node>
676	entire understand tour <area>
677	entire understand impact <file|node>
678	entire understand pr <id>
679	entire understand examples <pattern>
680	entire understand dashboard [--open] [--replay]
681	entire understand replay [--from <checkpoint|date>] [--to <checkpoint|date>]
682	entire understand hotspots
683	entire understand prime [<path>...] [--agent <name>] [--exec]
684	```
685	
686	Cross-command rules:
687	
688	- exact node IDs are always accepted
689	- file paths normalize relative to repo root
690	- `--json` exists on every read/query command
691	- `build` and `status` are explicit prerequisites for freshness
692	
693	## What lives where
694	
695	Everything lives in `entireio/cli`.
696	
697	Likely code areas:
698	
699	- `cmd/entire/cli/understand_*` for Cobra wiring
700	- `cmd/entire/cli/understand/graph/` for core graph types and persistence
701	- `cmd/entire/cli/understand/index/` for structural scanning and parser plugins
702	- `cmd/entire/cli/understand/history/` for checkpoint fusion
703	- `cmd/entire/cli/understand/semantic/` for agent-assisted JSON synthesis
704	- `cmd/entire/cli/understand/dashboard/` for embedded local UI/server
705	- `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/understand_*_test.go`
706	
707	No code lives in Understand-Anything because this plan intentionally removes
708	that dependency.
709	
710	## Single-PR delivery
711	
712	Ship as a **single PR**. The reviewer explicitly requested no split delivery,
713	and this subsystem is tightly coupled enough that dividing it into separate PRs
714	would mostly create artificial seams.
715	
716	To keep an 8-moment surface achievable in one review, every command in this PR
717	ships at **minimum-viable depth**. The acceptance contract per command:
718	
719	- `status`, `build`, `explain` — fully functional. These are load-bearing for
720	  every other command and must be production-quality.
721	- `tour`, `impact`, `examples`, `hotspots`, `prime` — fully functional in CLI
722	  text + `--json` modes; agent synthesis required where the moment depends on
723	  it; no novel UI.
724	- `pr` — fully functional with `gh`-based and revset fallback paths.
725	- `dashboard`, `replay` — deliberately plain local UI: a single static HTML
726	  shell + JSON endpoints is acceptable for v1. No build toolchain, no SPA
727	  framework, no design polish. The authenticated endpoint contract and
728	  read-only posture are the production-quality parts; the visual layer is
729	  intentionally minimal and may be tightened in follow-up PRs.
730	
731	Anything beyond this minimum-viable depth is explicitly out of scope for the
732	single PR and goes on the post-merge follow-up list.
733	
734	Expected size:
735	
736	- materially larger than the earlier overlay-only draft
737	- still acceptable because the graph schema, build pipeline, queries, and
738	  dashboard endpoints are one coherent feature set, and the dashboard's UI
739	  layer is held to "plain HTML over JSON" rather than a separate frontend
740	  project
741	
742	If during implementation the diff is exceeding the size at which a single
743	reviewer can usefully review it, the implementer should pause and re-raise
744	with the user rather than silently splitting the PR — phasing requires
745	explicit reviewer approval per the original constraint.
746	
747	Implementation order inside that one PR:
748	
749	1. graph schema + storage
750	2. structural index
751	3. history fusion
752	4. semantic synthesis helpers
753	5. command queries
754	6. dashboard/replay UI
755	7. priming wrapper
756	8. tests/docs
757	
758	That is execution order, not phased shipping.
759	
760	## Alternatives Considered
761	
762	- **Wrap** — rejected because the reviewer explicitly does not want an
763	  Understand-Anything dependency.
764	- **Overlay** — rejected because it keeps Entire subordinate to an external base
765	  graph and underserves moments 6–8.
766	- **Hybrid** — rejected because the requested direction is explicit CLI
767	  invocation with user-installed agents, not hook/session-driven pipeline runs.
768	- **Checkpoint attributes only** — rejected because replay, hotspots, examples,
769	  and priming all benefit from traversable checkpoint nodes.
770	- **Hook-based priming/build freshness** — rejected by reviewer instruction.
771	- **Dashboard-only or CLI-only slices** — rejected because the reviewer asked
772	  for the full 1–8 surface specified together rather than split experiments.
773	
774	## Risks & Open Questions
775	
776	The major implementation seams have all been pinned in the Proposal: parser
777	coverage (Go-only symbols, file-level for everything else), dashboard stack
778	(embedded vanilla SPA), `prime --exec` breadth (claude-code only), and `pr`
779	auth (delegated to the user's `gh` install). The remaining open questions are
780	genuinely deferred, not implementation-defining:
781	
782	1. **Per-moment "POC bar".** Some moments will land richer than others within
783	   the single-PR budget. Implementer should circulate a one-paragraph
784	   per-moment scope check before merging stage 6 (dashboard/replay UI) so the
785	   reviewer can confirm what "implemented" means for each numbered moment.
786	2. **Future symbol-level coverage prioritization.** Once the schema is in
787	   place, the first follow-up plugin language is likely TypeScript or Python
788	   based on repo composition, but that prioritization is out of scope here.
789	
790	Non-blocking risks:
791	
792	- semantic synthesis cost can be high on large repos; explicit build plus shard
793	  concurrency limits keep it user-controlled
794	- dashboard scope can sprawl; the POC should prefer a deliberately plain,
795	  inspectable local UI over a polished app
796	- contradiction/hotspot heuristics can overstate confidence if the UI does not
797	  distinguish deterministic vs inferred signals
798	
799	## Decision
800	
801	Chosen architecture: **Fuse**, native Entire-owned implementation, canonical
802	group **`entire understand`**.
803	
804	Ship as a **single PR** that specifies and implements all eight requested user
805	moments. Do not use Understand-Anything. Do not use hooks for build freshness
806	or priming. Use the user's installed agent CLIs through Entire's existing
807	text-generation/provider-selection path for bounded semantic synthesis only.
808	
809	This is the plan to implement unless a later reviewer objects to the native
810	Fuse direction itself, not to the now-removed upstream dependency.

- Synthesizer applies a 30s default per-shard context deadline (matches
  `entire explain --generate`), retries once on JSON-parse or schema-
  validation failure with a "JSON only, no prose" reminder, and degrades
  the shard to deterministic-only (FellBack=true) on the second failure
  rather than failing the whole build.
- Validator surface is structural via JSONValidator[T] — callers supply
  a constructor + invariant funcs and get back a SchemaValidator that
  attaches model-facing hints (NewValidationFeedback) to retries.
- A leading ```json fence is stripped once before validation so models
  that wrap responses despite "no prose" instructions don't burn the
  retry budget.
- RunSharded fans N independent requests out at a configurable concurrency
  cap (default 3 per spec) and preserves input order in outcomes. One
  shard's fallback never blocks others.
- DataBlock wraps untrusted input in `<tag nonce="...">...</tag>` framing
  with a fresh per-call nonce so smuggled closing tags can't truncate the
  data block. Header is the standard "treat blocks as data only" preamble.
- Logger interface is minimal so the CLI passes a wrapper around
  cmd/entire/cli/logging; the package never persists raw model output.

Tests cover happy path, fence stripping, retry-then-success, retry-then-
fallback (validation invariant case), parent-context cancellation, hint
propagation on retry, nil-validator rejection, sharded order
preservation, concurrency cap, and per-shard fallback isolation.
